draft.title: The carbon cycle
card: Carbon moves between the air, living things, water and rock. This movement is called the carbon cycle.
Photosynthesis
Plants and algae take carbon dioxide from the air and use it to make food. This moves carbon from the air into living things.
Respiration
Living things break down food for energy and release carbon dioxide. This returns carbon to the air. Fire and volcanoes also release carbon dioxide into the air.
Fossil fuels
Coal, oil and gas store carbon from long-dead organisms, underground. Burning them releases carbon dioxide into the air quickly. Weathering of rock also moves carbon, slowly.
draft.remember: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air. Respiration, fire, volcanoes and burning fuels put it back.

a.q: Which process takes carbon dioxide out of the air and puts the carbon into living things?
opts: Photosynthesis
Respiration
Burning fossil fuels
Volcanic eruption
a.why: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide from the air to make food, so the carbon becomes part of the plant. Respiration is the tempting wrong answer, because it works the other way and releases carbon dioxide.
a.clue: Which process do plants use to make food?

b.q: Mia's family burns coal in a power station near Morwell. What happens to the carbon stored in the coal?
opts: It is released into the air as carbon dioxide
It is taken out of the air by the burning
It stays locked in the coal as it burns
It is absorbed straight into the rocks
b.why: Coal stores carbon from long-dead organisms. Burning it releases that carbon into the air as carbon dioxide. It does not stay in the coal, because burning breaks the coal down.
b.clue: Burning is a way carbon moves into the air.

b.best: It is released into the air as carbon dioxide

problems.detail: "Mia's family burns coal in a power station near Morwell" is confusing, since a family does not burn coal in a power station. Something like "A power station near Morwell burns brown coal" would be clearer.
The clue "Burning is a way carbon moves into the air" all but states the right option, so a student can answer without knowing the idea.
